Habib Bourguiba led Tunisia to independence from France in 1956 and ruled it as its first president until 1987. He is the founder of modern Tunisia.

Born in Monastir and trained as a lawyer in Paris, he founded the Neo-Destour party in 1934 and spent years in French prisons. He favoured step-by-step bargaining over all-out war, unlike the fighters next door in Algeria.

In power he pushed through the Code of Personal Status, which banned polygamy and gave women rights unusual in the Arab world, built schools for all, and curbed the religious scholars of the Zaytuna. But he made himself president for life. Old and ill, he was removed in 1987 by his prime minister, Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali, who ruled until the revolution of 2011.
sum: Habib Bourguiba led Tunisia to independence from France in 1956 and ruled it as its first president until 1987. He is the founder of modern Tunisia.
